Mathematical definitions of the test problems

Source: vignettes/articles/problem-definitions.Rmd
problem-definitions.Rmd

Use this page to find the residual equations, supported dimensions, and standard starting point for any problem implemented by funconstrain. The definitions follow Section 3 of Moré, Garbow, and Hillstrom (1981) using one notation throughout. The authors’ Algorithm 566 source is a second primary source for resolving typographical and indexing ambiguities.

The formulas follow those sources; the dimensions and defaults describe the current package. Where funconstrain supports a narrower range, that range is shown. To run a problem, see Getting started with funconstrain or the funconstrain_problem() reference.

For x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in\mathbb{R}^n, every problem below defines m residuals. The scalar callback returned by the package is

F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{m}r_i(x)^2, \qquad \texttt{problem\$fn(x)}=F(x).

Indices in the equations are one-based. A sum over an empty index range is zero. x^{(0)} denotes the standard starting point.

1. Rosenbrock Function

Dimensions: n=2, m=2
Factory: rosen()

\begin{aligned} r_1(x)&=10(x_2-x_1^2),\\ r_2(x)&=1-x_1. \end{aligned}

Start: x^{(0)}=(-1.2,1)

2. Freudenstein and Roth Function

Dimensions: n=2, m=2
Factory: freud_roth()

\begin{aligned} r_1(x)&=-13+x_1+\{(5-x_2)x_2-2\}x_2,\\ r_2(x)&=-29+x_1+\{(1+x_2)x_2-14\}x_2. \end{aligned}

Start: x^{(0)}=(1/2,-2)

3. Powell Badly Scaled Function

Dimensions: n=2, m=2
Factory: powell_bs()

\begin{aligned} r_1(x)&=10^4x_1x_2-1,\\ r_2(x)&=e^{-x_1}+e^{-x_2}-1.0001. \end{aligned}

Start: x^{(0)}=(0,1)

4. Brown Badly Scaled Function

Dimensions: n=2, m=3
Factory: brown_bs()

\begin{aligned} r_1(x)&=x_1-10^6,\\ r_2(x)&=x_2-2\times10^{-6},\\ r_3(x)&=x_1x_2-2. \end{aligned}

Start: x^{(0)}=(1,1)

5. Beale Function

Dimensions: n=2, m=3
Factory: beale()

For i=1,2,3, let (c_1,c_2,c_3)=(1.5,2.25,2.625). Then

r_i(x)=c_i-x_1(1-x_2^i).

Start: x^{(0)}=(1,1)

6. Jennrich and Sampson Function

Dimensions: n=2, m\ge2; default m=10
Factory: jenn_samp()

For i=1,\ldots,m,

r_i(x)=2+2i-e^{ix_1}-e^{ix_2}.

Start: x^{(0)}=(0.3,0.4)

7. Helical Valley Function

Dimensions: n=3, m=3
Factory: helical()

Away from (x_1,x_2)=(0,0), define

\theta(x_1,x_2)= \begin{cases} \dfrac{1}{2\pi}\tan^{-1}(x_2/x_1),&x_1>0,\\ [4pt] \dfrac{1}{2\pi}\tan^{-1}(x_2/x_1)+\dfrac12,&x_1<0,\\ [4pt] \dfrac14\operatorname{sgn}(x_2),&x_1=0. \end{cases}

The residuals are

\begin{aligned} r_1(x)&=10\{x_3-10\theta(x_1,x_2)\},\\ r_2(x)&=10\{(x_1^2+x_2^2)^{1/2}-1\},\\ r_3(x)&=x_3. \end{aligned}

Implementation note: The package rejects the origin, where the objective is undefined.

Start: x^{(0)}=(-1,0,0)

8. Bard Function

Dimensions: n=3, m=15
Factory: bard()

For i=1,\ldots,15, set v_i=16-i, w_i=\min(i,v_i), and

\begin{aligned} (y_1,\ldots,y_{15})={}&(0.14,0.18,0.22,0.25,0.29,0.32,0.35,0.39,\\ &0.37,0.58,0.73,0.96,1.34,2.10,4.39). \end{aligned}

Then

r_i(x)=y_i-\left(x_1+\frac{i}{v_ix_2+w_ix_3}\right).

Start: x^{(0)}=(1,1,1)

9. Gaussian Function

Dimensions: n=3, m=15
Factory: gauss()

For i=1,\ldots,15, set t_i=(8-i)/2 and

\begin{aligned} (y_1,\ldots,y_{15})={}&(0.0009,0.0044,0.0175,0.0540,0.1295,\\ &0.2420,0.3521,0.3989,0.3521,0.2420,\\ &0.1295,0.0540,0.0175,0.0044,0.0009). \end{aligned}

Then

r_i(x)=x_1\exp\left\{-\frac{x_2}{2}(t_i-x_3)^2\right\}-y_i.

Start: x^{(0)}=(0.4,1,0)

10. Meyer Function

Dimensions: n=3, m=16
Factory: meyer()

For i=1,\ldots,16, set t_i=45+5i and

\begin{aligned} (y_1,\ldots,y_{16})={}&(34780,28610,23650,19630,16370,13720,11540,9744,\\ &8261,7030,6005,5147,4427,3820,3307,2872). \end{aligned}

Then

r_i(x)=x_1\exp\left(\frac{x_2}{t_i+x_3}\right)-y_i.

Start: x^{(0)}=(0.02,4000,250)

11. Gulf Research and Development Function

Dimensions: n=3, 3\le m\le100; default m=99
Factory: gulf()

For i=1,\ldots,m, define

t_i=\frac{i}{100},\qquad y_i=25+\{-50\log(t_i)\}^{2/3}.

The residual is

r_i(x)=\exp\left\{-\frac{|x_2-y_i|^{x_3}}{x_1}\right\}-t_i.

Source note: The published equation has a typographical glyph where the subtraction in |x_2-y_i| should appear; the corrected form above agrees with the authors’ Algorithm 566 source and the package.

Start: x^{(0)}=(5,2.5,0.15)

12. Box Three-Dimensional Function

Dimensions: n=3, m\ge3; default m=20
Factory: box_3d()

For i=1,\ldots,m, let t_i=i/10. Then

r_i(x)=e^{-t_ix_1}-e^{-t_ix_2}-x_3(e^{-t_i}-e^{-i}).

Start: x^{(0)}=(0,10,20)

13. Powell Singular Function

Dimensions: n=4, m=4
Factory: powell_s()

\begin{aligned} r_1(x)&=x_1+10x_2,\\ r_2(x)&=\sqrt5(x_3-x_4),\\ r_3(x)&=(x_2-2x_3)^2,\\ r_4(x)&=\sqrt{10}(x_1-x_4)^2. \end{aligned}

Start: x^{(0)}=(3,-1,0,1)

14. Wood Function

Dimensions: n=4, m=6
Factory: wood()

\begin{aligned} r_1(x)&=10(x_2-x_1^2),&r_2(x)&=1-x_1,\\ r_3(x)&=\sqrt{90}(x_4-x_3^2),&r_4(x)&=1-x_3,\\ r_5(x)&=\sqrt{10}(x_2+x_4-2),& r_6(x)&=(x_2-x_4)/\sqrt{10}. \end{aligned}

Start: x^{(0)}=(-3,-1,-3,-1)

15. Kowalik and Osborne Function

Dimensions: n=4, m=11
Factory: kow_osb()

The data are

\begin{aligned} (y_1,\ldots,y_{11})={}&(0.1957,0.1947,0.1735,0.1600,0.0844,0.0627,\\ &0.0456,0.0342,0.0323,0.0235,0.0246),\\ (u_1,\ldots,u_{11})={}&(4,2,1,0.5,0.25,0.167,0.125,0.1,\\ &0.0833,0.0714,0.0625). \end{aligned}

For i=1,\ldots,11,

r_i(x)=y_i-x_1\frac{u_i(u_i+x_2)}{u_i(u_i+x_3)+x_4}.

Start: x^{(0)}=(0.25,0.39,0.415,0.39)

16. Brown and Dennis Function

Dimensions: n=4, m\ge4; default m=20
Factory: brown_den()

For i=1,\ldots,m, let t_i=i/5 and define

\begin{aligned} a_i(x)&=x_1+t_ix_2-e^{t_i},\\ b_i(x)&=x_3+x_4\sin(t_i)-\cos(t_i),\\ r_i(x)&=a_i(x)^2+b_i(x)^2. \end{aligned}

Objective note: This problem squares a_i^2+b_i^2 once more in the shared objective F(x)=\sum_i r_i(x)^2.

Start: x^{(0)}=(25,5,-5,1)

17. Osborne 1 Function

Dimensions: n=5, m=33
Factory: osborne_1()

Let t_i=10(i-1) and define the observations in consecutive blocks:

\begin{aligned} (y_1,\ldots,y_8)&=(0.844,0.908,0.932,0.936,0.925,0.908,0.881,0.850),\\ (y_9,\ldots,y_{16})&=(0.818,0.784,0.751,0.718,0.685,0.658,0.628,0.603),\\ (y_{17},\ldots,y_{24})&=(0.580,0.558,0.538,0.522,0.506,0.490,0.478,0.467),\\ (y_{25},\ldots,y_{32})&=(0.457,0.448,0.438,0.431,0.424,0.420,0.414,0.411),\\ y_{33}&=0.406. \end{aligned}

For i=1,\ldots,33,

r_i(x)=y_i-\{x_1+x_2e^{-t_ix_4}+x_3e^{-t_ix_5}\}.

Start: x^{(0)}=(0.5,1.5,-1,0.01,0.02)

18. Biggs EXP6 Function

Dimensions: n=6, m\ge6; default m=13
Factory: biggs_exp6()

For i=1,\ldots,m, let t_i=i/10 and

y_i=e^{-t_i}-5e^{-10t_i}+3e^{-4t_i}.

Then

r_i(x)=x_3e^{-t_ix_1}-x_4e^{-t_ix_2}+x_6e^{-t_ix_5}-y_i.

Start: x^{(0)}=(1,2,1,1,1,1)

19. Osborne 2 Function

Dimensions: n=11, m=65
Factory: osborne_2()

Let t_i=(i-1)/10. The observations, in consecutive blocks, are

\begin{aligned} (y_1,\ldots,y_8)&=(1.366,1.191,1.112,1.013,0.991,0.885,0.831,0.847),\\ (y_9,\ldots,y_{16})&=(0.786,0.725,0.746,0.679,0.608,0.655,0.616,0.606),\\ (y_{17},\ldots,y_{24})&=(0.602,0.626,0.651,0.724,0.649,0.649,0.694,0.644),\\ (y_{25},\ldots,y_{32})&=(0.624,0.661,0.612,0.558,0.533,0.495,0.500,0.423),\\ (y_{33},\ldots,y_{40})&=(0.395,0.375,0.372,0.391,0.396,0.405,0.428,0.429),\\ (y_{41},\ldots,y_{48})&=(0.523,0.562,0.607,0.653,0.672,0.708,0.633,0.668),\\ (y_{49},\ldots,y_{56})&=(0.645,0.632,0.591,0.559,0.597,0.625,0.739,0.710),\\ (y_{57},\ldots,y_{64})&=(0.729,0.720,0.636,0.581,0.428,0.292,0.162,0.098),\\ y_{65}&=0.054. \end{aligned}

For i=1,\ldots,65,

\begin{aligned} r_i(x)=y_i-&\{x_1e^{-t_ix_5}+x_2e^{-x_6(t_i-x_9)^2}\\ &+x_3e^{-x_7(t_i-x_{10})^2}+x_4e^{-x_8(t_i-x_{11})^2}\}. \end{aligned}

Start: x^{(0)}=(1.3,0.65,0.65,0.7,0.6,3,5,7,2,4.5,5.5)

20. Watson Function

Dimensions: 2\le n\le31, m=31; default n=6
Factory: watson()

For i=1,\ldots,29, define

\begin{aligned} t_i&=i/29,\\ a_i(x)&=\sum_{j=2}^{n}(j-1)x_jt_i^{j-2},\\ b_i(x)&=\sum_{j=1}^{n}x_jt_i^{j-1}. \end{aligned}

The residuals are

\begin{aligned} r_i(x)&=a_i(x)-b_i(x)^2-1,&&i=1,\ldots,29,\\ r_{30}(x)&=x_1,\\ r_{31}(x)&=x_2-x_1^2-1. \end{aligned}

Start: x^{(0)}=(0,\ldots,0)

21. Extended Rosenbrock Function

Dimensions: even n\ge2, m=n; default n=8
Factory: ex_rosen()

For k=1,\ldots,n/2,

\begin{aligned} r_{2k-1}(x)&=10(x_{2k}-x_{2k-1}^2),\\ r_{2k}(x)&=1-x_{2k-1}. \end{aligned}

Start: Repeat (-1.2,1) exactly n/2 times.

22. Extended Powell Function

Dimensions: n\ge4 and divisible by 4, m=n; default n=20
Factory: ex_powell()

For k=1,\ldots,n/4, let a=4k-3. Then

\begin{aligned} r_a(x)&=x_a+10x_{a+1},\\ r_{a+1}(x)&=\sqrt5(x_{a+2}-x_{a+3}),\\ r_{a+2}(x)&=(x_{a+1}-2x_{a+2})^2,\\ r_{a+3}(x)&=\sqrt{10}(x_a-x_{a+3})^2. \end{aligned}

Naming note: MGH calls this the “Extended Powell singular” problem; the package title is shortened.

Start: Repeat (3,-1,0,1) exactly n/4 times.

23. Penalty Function I

Dimensions: n\ge1, m=n+1; default n=25
Factory: penalty_1()

With a=10^{-5},

\begin{aligned} r_j(x)&=\sqrt{a}(x_j-1),&&j=1,\ldots,n,\\ r_{n+1}(x)&=\sum_{j=1}^{n}x_j^2-\frac14. \end{aligned}

Start: x_j^{(0)}=j

24. Penalty Function II

Dimensions: n\ge1, m=2n; default n=25
Factory: penalty_2()

With a=10^{-5}, the residuals are

\begin{aligned} r_1(x)&=x_1-0.2,\\ r_i(x)&=\sqrt a\{e^{x_i/10}+e^{x_{i-1}/10}-e^{i/10}-e^{(i-1)/10}\}, &&i=2,\ldots,n,\\ r_{n+i-1}(x)&=\sqrt a\{e^{x_i/10}-e^{-0.1}\}, &&i=2,\ldots,n,\\ r_{2n}(x)&=\sum_{j=1}^{n}(n-j+1)x_j^2-1. \end{aligned}

Edge case: For n=1, the two middle ranges are empty.

Start: x_j^{(0)}=1/2

25. Variably Dimensioned Function

Dimensions: n\ge1, m=n+2; default n=30
Factory: var_dim()

Define s(x)=\sum_{j=1}^{n}j(x_j-1). Then

\begin{aligned} r_j(x)&=x_j-1,&&j=1,\ldots,n,\\ r_{n+1}(x)&=s(x),\\ r_{n+2}(x)&=s(x)^2. \end{aligned}

Start: x_j^{(0)}=1-j/n

26. Trigonometric Function

Dimensions: n\ge1, m=n; default n=30
Factory: trigon()

For i=1,\ldots,n,

r_i(x)=n-\sum_{j=1}^{n}\cos(x_j)+i\{1-\cos(x_i)\}-\sin(x_i).

Start: x_j^{(0)}=1/n

27. Brown Almost-Linear Function

Dimensions: n\ge1, m=n; default n=30
Factory: brown_al()

\begin{aligned} r_i(x)&=x_i+\sum_{j=1}^{n}x_j-(n+1),&&i=1,\ldots,n-1,\\ r_n(x)&=\prod_{j=1}^{n}x_j-1. \end{aligned}

Edge case: For n=1, the first range is empty.

Start: x_j^{(0)}=1/2

28. Discrete Boundary Value Function

Dimensions: n\ge1, m=n; default n=35
Factory: disc_bv()

Let h=1/(n+1), t_i=ih, and set the boundary values x_0=x_{n+1}=0. For i=1,\ldots,n,

r_i(x)=2x_i-x_{i-1}-x_{i+1}+\frac{h^2}{2}(x_i+t_i+1)^3.

Start: x_i^{(0)}=t_i(t_i-1)

29. Discrete Integral Equation Function

Dimensions: n\ge1, m=n; default n=35
Factory: disc_ie()

Let h=1/(n+1), t_i=ih, and q_j(x)=(x_j+t_j+1)^3. For i=1,\ldots,n,

r_i(x)=x_i+\frac{h}{2}\left\{ (1-t_i)\sum_{j=1}^{i}t_jq_j(x) +t_i\sum_{j=i+1}^{n}(1-t_j)q_j(x) \right\}.

Start: x_i^{(0)}=t_i(t_i-1)

30. Broyden Tridiagonal Function

Dimensions: n\ge1, m=n; default n=40
Factory: broyden_tri()

Set x_0=x_{n+1}=0. For i=1,\ldots,n,

r_i(x)=(3-2x_i)x_i-x_{i-1}-2x_{i+1}+1.

Start: x^{(0)}=(-1,\ldots,-1)

31. Broyden Banded Function

Dimensions: n\ge1, m=n; default n=40
Factory: broyden_band()

For each i=1,\ldots,n, define

B_i=\{j:\max(1,i-5)\le j\le\min(n,i+1),\ j\ne i\}.

Then

r_i(x)=x_i(2+5x_i^2)+1-\sum_{j\in B_i}x_j(1+x_j).

Start: x^{(0)}=(-1,\ldots,-1)

32. Linear Function - Full Rank

Dimensions: n\ge1, m\ge n; defaults n=45, m=100
Factory: linfun_fr()

Define c(x)=1+(2/m)\sum_{j=1}^{n}x_j. Then

r_i(x)= \begin{cases} x_i-c(x),&i=1,\ldots,n,\\ -c(x),&i=n+1,\ldots,m. \end{cases}

Start: x^{(0)}=(1,\ldots,1)

33. Linear Function - Rank 1

Dimensions: n\ge1, m\ge n; defaults n=45, m=100
Factory: linfun_r1()

For i=1,\ldots,m,

r_i(x)=i\sum_{j=1}^{n}jx_j-1.

Start: x^{(0)}=(1,\ldots,1)

34. Linear Function - Rank 1 with Zero Columns and Rows

Dimensions: n\ge1, m\ge n; defaults n=45, m=100
Factory: linfun_r1z()

Define s(x)=\sum_{j=2}^{n-1}jx_j. The residuals are

\begin{aligned} r_1(x)&=-1,\\ r_i(x)&=(i-1)s(x)-1,&&i=2,\ldots,m-1,\\ r_m(x)&=-1. \end{aligned}

Edge case: For n\le2, the sum defining s(x) is empty.

Start: x^{(0)}=(1,\ldots,1)

35. Chebyquad Function

Dimensions: n\ge1, m\ge n; default n=50 and m=n
Factory: chebyquad()

Let T_i^*(u)=T_i(2u-1) be the Chebyshev polynomial shifted to [0,1], with

\begin{aligned} T_0^*(u)&=1,\\ T_1^*(u)&=2u-1,\\ T_i^*(u)&=2(2u-1)T_{i-1}^*(u)-T_{i-2}^*(u). \end{aligned}

For i=1,\ldots,m,

r_i(x)=\frac1n\sum_{j=1}^{n}T_i^*(x_j)-c_i, \qquad c_i= \begin{cases} 0,&i\text{ odd},\\ -1/(i^2-1),&i\text{ even}. \end{cases}

Calling chebyquad() derives m=n from the parameter-vector length. Pass an explicit m to the factory to use an overdetermined instance with m>n.

Start: x_j^{(0)}=j/(n+1)
